# Solo Satoshi Bitaxe and NerdAxe Web Flasher

Canonical URL: https://flash.solosatoshi.com/
Operator: Solo Satoshi LLC
Application license: GNU GPL version 3 only
Application source: https://flash.solosatoshi.com/source/latest.tar.gz

## Purpose

The Solo Satoshi Web Flasher installs current factory firmware on supported Bitaxe and NerdAxe Bitcoin miners from a compatible desktop web browser. It is designed for Chrome, Edge, and Brave browsers with Web Serial support.

## Installation process

1. Connect the miner with a data-capable USB cable and approve its USB serial device when prompted by the browser.
2. Choose the Bitaxe or NerdAxe firmware family.
3. Choose the latest-release or prerelease channel.
4. Select the exact miner model.
5. Select the board revision printed on Bitaxe hardware. The flasher matches this value automatically for NerdAxe models without showing a redundant board dropdown.
6. Select a compatible production firmware version. Prerelease mode uses the current eligible prerelease for the selected hardware.
7. Choose whether to preserve the miner's saved Wi-Fi, pool, and configuration settings.
8. Start the installation and keep USB and power connected until flashing and the automatic restart are complete.

The interface presents these eight steps in matching rows and enforces their dependencies. Miner-family selection requires USB approval, model selection requires a confirmed release channel, board matching requires a model, firmware selection requires a supported board, and settings and installation remain disabled until a compatible firmware image is selected. When no eligible prerelease exists, the prerelease option remains visible but disabled and the latest-release channel is selected automatically.

## Custom firmware

The installer provides Verified releases and Advanced tabs. The Advanced tab accepts a local merged ESP32-S3 `.bin` built for address `0x0`. It checks the ESP boot-image header, the partition table at `0x8000`, the file size, and the locally calculated SHA-256 digest. A file can be selected and validated before USB connection, while flashing remains disabled until both a valid file and a miner connection are present. The custom file remains in browser memory and is never uploaded. Because there is no trusted release digest or hardware-compatibility record for a user-supplied image, the tool writes the complete image without preserving settings and identifies it as unverified custom firmware.

## Firmware integrity

Firmware is discovered from the official ESP-Miner repositories for the supported device families. Automated release processing checks each file against the digest published by GitHub. After a compatible version is selected, the browser prepares the matching image and independently verifies its SHA-256 checksum before writing it to the device. Changing the hardware or version prepares the newly matched image. A verified image may be reused from page memory or the browser HTTP cache. The interface links to the upstream release and a corresponding source archive.

## Supported hardware

The live manifest determines the exact supported images. The displayed families include Bitaxe models such as Gamma, Gamma Duo, Gamma Turbo, Hex, Max, Supra, SupraHex, Ultra, GammaHex, and Naja Duo, plus supported NerdAxe, NerdAxe Gamma, NerdEKO, NerdHaxe, NerdOCTAXE, NerdQAxe, NerdQX, Q1370, and Q1373 revisions. Users must match the exact board identifier printed on their device.

## Privacy

The application has no account system and does not request names, email addresses, payment details, private keys, seed phrases, wallet credentials, Wi-Fi passwords, or mining pool credentials. It does not use advertising cookies or behavioral analytics. It stores the selected language in localStorage, does not use sessionStorage, and may use the browser-managed HTTP cache for verified firmware files. Web Serial access requires an explicit browser selection. The application does not upload USB logs, miner settings, or locally selected custom firmware files to Solo Satoshi. Hosting and delivery providers receive ordinary network request information needed to operate and secure the service.

Privacy policy: https://flash.solosatoshi.com/privacy.html

## Open-source relationship

ESP-Miner and related firmware are community-developed open-source projects. Solo Satoshi may sponsor, test, document, package, distribute, or contribute code and also sells compatible hardware. Solo Satoshi is not the sole author or controller of every upstream release or third-party contribution.
